tags.description:
Ready-made connectors and how their fields map to JobMojito. A company sees the same tables under Integrations > Catalogue > Field mapping.

### ATS connector (Kombo)

The applicant tracking system is connected through Kombo's unified ATS API. JobMojito keeps a copy of the ATS jobs, applications and candidates, links each position to one ATS job, invites applicants who reach the trigger stage, and writes the outcome back. Links, notes and attachments are written only when the company switched them on (merchant.kombo_selected_result_actions); job fields are not copied into the position.

| JobMojito field | Direction | External field | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant.kombo_integration_id, merchant.kombo_integration_tool` | Into JobMojito | `integration-created / integration-deleted webhook: data.id, data.tool` | Set when the ATS connection is created and cleared when it is deleted. |
| `kombo_jobs.id, kombo_jobs.name` | Into JobMojito | `GET /ats/jobs: id, name (fallback title)` | Copied on every full or incremental sync of the jobs. |
| `kombo_jobs.status` | Into JobMojito | `jobs.status, jobs.remote_deleted_at` | DRAFT becomes draft, CLOSED or ARCHIVED becomes archived, deleted in the ATS becomes deleted. |
| `kombo_jobs.data` | Into JobMojito | `jobs.* (whole job object)` | Kept as received; the position's own fields are not overwritten from it. |
| `position_def_set.kombo_parameters.kombo_job_id, interview_def_set.kombo_parameters.kombo_job_id` | Into JobMojito | `jobs.id` | Links a position or interview to one ATS job, chosen by the recruiter. |
| `position_def_set.status, interview_def_set.status` | Into JobMojito | `jobs.status (closed, archived, deleted, reopened)` | Closing the job in the ATS archives the linked positions and interviews; reopening it restores their previous status. |
| `kombo_parameters.kombo_stage_id` | Into JobMojito | `jobs.stages[].id matched against applications.current_stage_id` | An application entering this stage triggers the invitation or the pre-screening; applicants already in it are invited when the position is published. |
| `ATS pipeline report (stage names and order)` | Into JobMojito | `jobs.stages[].id, name, index` | Read for the ATS pipeline report only. |
| `kombo_applications.id, kombo_job_id, kombo_candidate_id, data` | Into JobMojito | `GET /ats/applications: id, job_id, candidate_id` | Copied on application sync; applications of closed or archived jobs are not imported. |
| `kombo_applications.kombo_stage_id` | Into JobMojito | `applications.current_stage_id` | A stage change re-runs the invitation check for that application. |
| `kombo_applications.status` | Into JobMojito | `applications.outcome (HIRED, DECLINED), remote_deleted_at` | Hired, declined or deleted applications are archived and receive no further invitations. |
| `position_result.outcome, interview_result.outcome` | Into JobMojito | `applications.outcome` | Set to hired or declined when the ATS marks the linked application, while the outcome is still pending. |
| `position_result.status, interview_result.status` | Into JobMojito | `applications.remote_deleted_at` | An application deleted in the ATS archives the linked application in JobMojito if nobody has decided yet. |
| `kombo_candidates.id, data, status` | Into JobMojito | `GET /ats/candidates: candidates.*, remote_deleted_at` | Copied on candidate sync; a candidate deleted in the ATS is archived. |
| `profile_interview.email, profile_interview.email_auth` | Into JobMojito | `candidates.email_addresses[0].email_address` | Finds or creates the candidate when the application reaches the trigger stage. |
| `profile_interview.name` | Into JobMojito | `candidates.first_name + last_name` | Set when the candidate is created from the ATS. |
| `profile_interview.phone_number` | Into JobMojito | `candidates.phone_numbers[0].phone_number` | Set when the candidate is created from the ATS. |
| `kombo_candidates.profile_interview_id` | Into JobMojito | `candidates.id (matched by e-mail)` | Links the ATS candidate to the JobMojito candidate on invitation or pre-screening. |
| `interview_file (type resume)` | Into JobMojito | `GET /ats/applications/{id}/attachments, then /ats/candidates/{id}/attachments: type CV (fallback OTHER)` | The CV from the ATS is imported when the candidate is invited or pre-screened. |
| `interview_result_pre_screening (AI pre-screening input)` | Into JobMojito | `applications.screening_question_answers[] (question.title, answer)` | The candidate's answers to the ATS screening questions are part of the AI pre-screening. |
| `interview_result_pre_screening.nationality, residency` | Into JobMojito | `candidates.location.country (fallback address.country)` | Taken from the ATS candidate during pre-screening. |
| `kombo_applications.interview_result_id, interview_result_pre_screening_id` | Into JobMojito | `applications.id` | Set when the candidate's result is linked back to the ATS application. |
| `kombo_tags, kombo_rejection_reasons, kombo_users, kombo_offers, kombo_interviews` | Into JobMojito | `GET /ats/tags, /ats/rejection-reasons, /ats/users, /ats/offers, /ats/interviews` | Kept in sync so recruiters can pick tags and rejection reasons; the others are stored only. |
| `kombo_parameters.kombo_selected_stage_id (step: config.kombo.accept_stage_id)` | From JobMojito | `PUT /ats/applications/{id}/stage` | Moves the application when the recruiter selects the candidate; the position's stage is used on the last step. |
| `kombo_parameters.kombo_sync_all_results_stage_id` | From JobMojito | `PUT /ats/applications/{id}/stage` | Every processed result is moved to this stage, only when sync all results is on. |
| `kombo_parameters.kombo_rejected_reason_human_id, kombo_rejected_reason_ai_id (step: config.kombo.reject_reason_id)` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/reject { rejection_reason_id, note }` | Rejects the application when the recruiter rejects; nothing is sent when no reason is configured. |
| `Rejection note (result link, score, AI feedback)` | From JobMojito | `reject.note` | The note sent with the rejection. |
| `interview_result result link + interview_result.score` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/result-links { label, url, details.attributes }` | Sent when result links are switched on: a signed link to the result with its score. |
| `interview_result note (result link + score)` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/notes` | Sent when notes are switched on and the recruiter has decided, or sync all results is on. |
| `interview_result.pdf_export_url (interview PDF report)` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/attachments (type OTHER)` | Sent when attachments are switched on; the PDF is generated first if missing. |
| `interview_result_pre_screening score, recommendation and analysis` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/notes` | Sent after every AI pre-screening and again when the recruiter decides on it. |
| `Pre-screening PDF report` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/attachments (type OTHER)` | Uploaded when attachments are switched on. |
| `interview_result.coach_status (progress note)` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/applications/{id}/notes` | A note when the interview fails or the answers are collected, only when sync all results is on. |
| `position_result_step decision and recruiter notes (meeting step)` | From JobMojito | `POST notes, PUT stage, POST reject` | Sends '<step>: passed / failed' with the recruiter's notes, then moves or rejects. |
| `human_interview_request reason and outcome` | From JobMojito | `POST notes, PUT stage, POST reject` | Notes the request, moves on pass and rejects on fail or decline. |
| `merchant.kombo_tag_assignment.result_weak / result_moderate / result_strong / result_exceptional` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/candidates/{id}/tags` | Score tags on result sync: under 4 weak, under 7 moderate, under 8.5 strong, up to 10 exceptional. |
| `merchant.kombo_tag_assignment.interview_selected / interview_rejected` | From JobMojito | `POST /ats/candidates/{id}/tags` | Decision tags on a recruiter decision; the selected tag only on the last step. |
| `merchant.kombo_sync (manual sync)` | From JobMojito | `POST /force-sync` | Asks Kombo to sync the ATS again when the recruiter presses sync. |

### Webhooks

JobMojito POSTs the same JSON payload for the events interview_result (the result is final and scored, sent again when a watched field changes), interview_collected (the candidate finished, before scoring) and interview_failed (failed, abandoned or no speech). Configure the URL, events and authentication headers per environment under Integrations > Custom integration; failed deliveries are retried and kept in the delivery history.

| JobMojito field | Direction | External field | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `interview_result.id` | From JobMojito | `id` | The result the event is about. |
| `interview_result.question_set_id (interview_def_set.id)` | From JobMojito | `interview_id` | The interview definition. |
| `interview_result.question_set_id (interview_def_set.id)` | From JobMojito | `question_set_id` | Same value as interview_id. |
| `interview_result.status` | From JobMojito | `status` | active for interview_result, draft for the other two events. |
| `interview_result.coach_status` | From JobMojito | `interview_status` | completed, failed, abandoned and so on. |
| `interview_result.processing_status` | From JobMojito | `processing_status` | AI processing state. |
| `interview_result.profile_interview_id` | From JobMojito | `profile_interview_id` | The candidate. |
| `interview_result.profile_id` | From JobMojito | `profile_id` | The candidate's portal account, when there is one. |
| `profile_interview.external_id` | From JobMojito | `candidate_external_id` | Your id for the candidate; present when a candidate is linked. |
| `profile_interview.name` | From JobMojito | `candidate_name` | Present when a candidate is linked. |
| `profile_interview.email` | From JobMojito | `candidate_email` | Present when a candidate is linked. |
| `profile_interview.phone_number` | From JobMojito | `candidate_phone_number` | Present when a candidate is linked. |
| `interview_result.recruiter_go_next_round` | From JobMojito | `recruiter_go_next_round` | The recruiter's decision; usually empty in interview_collected and interview_failed. |
| `interview_result.ai_analysis` | From JobMojito | `ai_analysis` | Candidate-facing analysis, filled in interview_result. |
| `interview_result.ai_analysis_recruiter` | From JobMojito | `ai_analysis_recruiter` | Recruiter-facing analysis, filled in interview_result. |
| `interview_result.ai_analysis_other` | From JobMojito | `ai_analysis_other` | Session analyses by name, for example strengths_concerns. |
| `interview_result.ai_analysis_other.strengths_concerns.strengths` | From JobMojito | `ai_analysis_recruiter_why_hire` | Deprecated copy kept for existing integrations. |
| `interview_result.ai_analysis_other.strengths_concerns.concerns` | From JobMojito | `ai_analysis_recruiter_why_not_hire` | Deprecated copy kept for existing integrations. |
| `interview_result.score_interview_ai` | From JobMojito | `ai_analysis_recruiter_score` | Recruiter-facing AI score, filled in interview_result. |
| `interview_result.score` | From JobMojito | `score` | Overall score, filled in interview_result. |
| `interview_result.pdf_export_url` | From JobMojito | `pdf_export_url` | When a PDF report is configured, interview_result waits until the PDF exists. |
| `Changed fields of the result` | From JobMojito | `reason` | Which watched fields changed; 'manual re-trigger of ...' on a resend from the delivery history. |

interview_def_set_id.description: Id of the newly created interview definition set.

embed_id.description: Embed id, present only when is_embedded=true.

embed_signing_key.description: Embed signing key, present only when is_embedded=true.

questions_generated.description: Number of questions actually generated (with questions: the number of questions you sent). May be lower than the requested interview_length, which is capped by max_duration.

max_duration.description: Live session limit in seconds stored on the interview — the value sent, or the 1200 default when omitted.

JobInterviewCreateResponse.description: Id of the created interview, the number of questions generated and the stored max_duration. Includes embed_id/embed_signing_key when is_embedded=true.

question.description: The question text shown to the candidate.

id.description: Identifier for this question. job-interview-get returns the question's real id here; send it back to job-interview-update so an unchanged question keeps its existing record (and with it its answer rules and any rendered avatar video). Also the handle another question references via conditional_question_main_id. On job-interview-create-from-array it is a caller-local value, only needed for those references.

duration.description: Answer duration in seconds for this question.

mojito_language_code.description: Per-question language override (one of the listed codes). Inherits the interview language when omitted.

label.description: Optional label/tag stored on the question.

is_conditional.description: A yes/no question that decides which follow-ups are asked (view 'with listening conditional'). Its follow-ups point at it with conditional_question_main_id.

is_without_scoring.description: Question is asked but not scored (view 'without scoring').

conditional_question_main_id.description: For a follow-up question, the id (the "id" field above) of the yes/no question (is_conditional) in this same array that decides whether it is asked. The yes/no question must appear earlier in the array. Use conditional_question_answer to choose the answer that shows it.

conditional_question_answer.description: With conditional_question_main_id: the answer to the yes/no question that shows this follow-up. `true` (the default) asks it after a yes, `false` after a no, so each answer can lead to its own follow-ups. Ignored on a question without conditional_question_main_id.

is_skippable.description: The candidate may skip this question: the recorded (offline avatar) interview shows a Skip button on it, and a skipped question is saved without an answer. Defaults to false.

knowledge_base_id.description: Knowledge-base store id (uuid) the question draws context from.

external_id.description: External identifier stored on the question. job-interview-update matches on this first, so an ATS that owns stable ids can send its own array and have the diff line up without round-tripping our ids.

external_data.description: Arbitrary JSON metadata stored on the question.

weak.description: Baseline requirements every viable candidate should meet (table stakes).

moderate.description: Requirements expected of a solid, competent candidate.

strong.description: High-bar requirements only standout candidates clear.

candidate_expectations_json.description: Per-question candidate expectations, bucketed by requirement level (weak/moderate/strong). Extra keys are preserved.

location.description: Job location — a city/country, or `remote`. Required and must not be empty: when the job description gives no location, pass `Not specified`.

interview_template_id.description: Id of the interview template to base this interview on.

mojito_language_code.description: Platform language code used for the interview. One of the listed codes.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the interview. Options — `draft`: Created but not published — not visible to candidates and cannot be run yet. Use to stage an interview before going live. | `active`: Published and live — candidates can run it.

type.description: Product type of the interview. Options — `interview`: Standard candidate interview for a role — answers are AI-scored as input for the reviewer's decision. | `coaching`: Practice/coaching session — candidate-facing feedback to help them improve; not a hiring evaluation. Only available on the coaching portal, NOT the interview portal. | `assessment`: Skills/knowledge assessment — evaluates competencies and is scored like an interview.

visibility.description: Who can discover and access the interview. Options — `merchant_public`: Listed on the merchant's public interview list — anyone with the merchant link can find and start it. | `merchant_invite`: Invite-only — only candidates explicitly invited (by email/link) can access it; not listed anywhere. | `merchant_unlisted`: Reachable only via a direct link — not listed anywhere; share the link manually.

recording.description: Cheating/proctoring detection mode for candidate answers — this is NOT a full session recording. Video options also record the candidate. Omit, null or `none` to disable. Options — `audio_first_5_answers`: Audio-only cheating detection, first 5 answers only. | `audio_all`: Audio-only cheating detection on every answer. | `video_all`: Audio + video cheating detection on every answer (candidate is recorded for all answers). | `video_first_5_answers`: Audio + video cheating detection, first 5 answers only. | `none`: No cheating detection.

recording_full_session.description: Full interview-session recording (includes the avatar and voice) produced as a single file. Independent of `recording`. Omit, null or `none` to disable. Options — `audio_all`: Record the whole session audio (avatar + candidate voice) into a single file. Adds +0.2 credits. | `video_all`: Record the whole session video + audio (avatar + candidate) into a single file. Adds +0.4 credits. | `none`: No full-session recording.

environment.description: Which of your webhook environments results from this interview are delivered to. Defaults to production. Options — `production`: Live hiring. Results reach the webhooks configured as production. This is the default when the field is omitted. | `uat`: User-acceptance testing - an isolated environment for pre-release verification. | `development`: Development/testing. Use for interviews created by a test or preview app so their results never reach the production webhook. | `demo`: Demonstrations and sales trials.

interview_type.description: Interview style — configures the AI avatar and shapes both the AI-generated questions and the follow-up questions asked during the interview. Defaults to pre-screening when omitted. Options — `pre-screening`: Pre-screening — quick qualification check focusing on basic requirements and availability. | `pre-screening-with-test-questions`: Pre-screening with test questions — pre-screening plus practical questions to test relevant skills. | `second-interview`: Second round interview — deeper dive for candidates who passed initial screening. | `remote-freelancer-verification`: Remote worker verification — verify remote work capabilities and communication skills. | `strength-based-interview`: Strength-based interview — focus on what candidates enjoy and excel at to predict job satisfaction. | `potential-based-interview`: Potential-based interview — assess learning ability and growth potential rather than past experience. | `process-verification-from-knowledge-base`: Knowledge Base interview — generate questions from your knowledge base documents. | `knockout-screening`: Knock-out screening — a short (about 5 minute) check of the role's must-haves with closed questions; ends early, politely, when a must-have is clearly not met. On creation it defaults custom_scoring.early_stop to true (where the avatar supports early stop) and max_followups to 1 unless you send them.

seniority_level.description: Target seniority level for the role; auto-detected from the job description when omitted. Options — `entry-level`: Early-career or graduate roles. | `intermediate`: Some experience required. | `senior`: Experienced professional. | `managerial`: Team or department lead. | `director`: Director-level responsibility. | `executive`: C-suite or executive role.

result_view.description: Result screen shown to the candidate after finishing. With any value other than `none`, the candidate sees a results screen where they can provide feedback, record an intro video and edit the transcript, and must then submit the result; the value sets how much score/result detail is shown. Options — `none`: No results screen at all — the interview is submitted immediately when the candidate finishes (no feedback, intro video, transcript edit or manual submit step). | `minimal`: Minimal results layout, no score shown. | `minimal_with_score`: Minimal results layout including the overall score. | `advanced`: Advanced results layout with more detail. | `full`: Full results layout with all sections. | `full_expand_scores`: Full results with every score breakdown expanded.

interview_conversation_speed.description: Conversation pace of the AI avatar. Omit/null keeps the template default pace. Options — `slower`: The avatar speaks more slowly — easier to follow for non-native speakers. | `normal`: Default speaking pace. | `faster`: The avatar speaks more quickly for a snappier conversation. | `fluent`: Talking pace: the avatar answers 300 ms after the candidate stops speaking. A pause mid-sentence also ends their turn.

candidate_video_introduction.description: Whether a candidate video introduction is optional or required.

interview_tone.description: Interview tone — configures the AI avatar's speaking style and the tone of the AI-generated questions and follow-ups. Case-insensitive; omit to default to relaxed. Options — `relaxed`: Friendly and conversational tone that helps candidates feel at ease. | `simple`: Plain language at CEFR A2 level — short sentences and simple words. | `professional`: Formal and business-like approach suitable for senior roles. | `persuasive`: Engaging style that encourages candidates to elaborate. | `exact`: Asks the questions exactly as provided, without rephrasing — for interviews built from your own questions where the wording is a script.

interview_length.description: Number of questions to generate (1-40). Also capped by max_duration, which allows one question per 2 minutes: 20 min -> 10 questions, 30 min -> 15, 45 min -> 22, 60 min -> 30, 80 min -> 40. Asking for more than the cap is not an error — you get the cap, and the response reports the real count in questions_generated. Omit this field to let the AI pick 5-8.

max_duration.description: Maximum interview duration in seconds. Scopes how many questions are generated (see interview_length) and is stored on the interview as the live session limit and the basis for the credit multiplier. Defaults to 1200 (20 minutes) when omitted.

max_followups.description: Maximum number of AI follow-up questions. 0 disables follow-ups; presets are 0-3 (none/low/normal/high) and custom values start at 4; null uses the template default (Normal).

questions_random_subset.description: Ask only a random subset of the questions, expressed as a fraction between 0.01 and 0.9 (e.g. 0.5 = 50%). null asks all questions.

code.description: Optional external code/reference for the interview.

interview_salary.description: Salary range shown for the position.

interview_available_till.description: ISO date/time after which the interview is no longer available to candidates. null keeps it always available.

recruiter_profile_id.description: Profile id of the recruiter owning this interview. A user of the company who is not read only: an owner, recruiter or admin from merchant-user-list.

name.description: End-employer name. Omit/null when hiring for yourself, 'undisclosed' for an unnamed external client, or the client's company name.

description.description: Short description of the end employer, used as background context by the agent.
description.example: Unimo Enterprises is a leading logistics and supply chain solutions provider.

location.description: Primary location of the end employer.

sector.description: Industry / sector of the end employer.

company_size.description: Approximate headcount of the end employer.

hiring_for_company.description: Who the position is really for. Omit/null (or an object with name null/blank) when hiring for yourself; { name: 'undisclosed' } for an unnamed external client; or { name: '<company>' } plus optional description/location/sector/company_size for a named client. Stored in creation_parameters.hiring_for_company.

tags.description: Free-form tags stored on the interview. Tags are also the coaching-catalogue mapping key: a catalogue directory (see the catalogue-tag-create / catalogue-tag-update endpoints) lists a coaching or persona session when the session's tags contain EVERY tag in that directory's `tags_interview_set_filter`. Only `active` sessions with visibility `merchant_public` (or the platform's own `public`) are listed.

merchant_id.description: Merchant id. Admin / sub-merchant callers only; otherwise taken from your token.

knowledge_base_store_id.description: Knowledge base store id to source additional context from. Documents limited to chosen interviews are left out, because a new interview is on no list yet.

description.description: Short, two-sentence job description shown to the candidate. Required with `questions`. Without `questions`, provide it to use it as-is, or leave it null/blank and it is AI-generated from the position name and any other context.
description.example: Backend role focused on Python, async APIs, and AWS.

description_long.description: Full job description in Markdown (Job Purpose, Responsibilities, Required & Preferred Qualifications). Provide it to use it as-is; leave it null/blank and it is AI-generated (interview and assessment types only). Rendered as Markdown on the candidate-facing position page, including chips, callouts, cards, columns and buttons — formatting guide: https://developer.jobmojito.com/cookbooks/format-content-with-markdown

candidate_expectations.description: Free-text candidate expectations folded into AI generation.

welcome_message.description: Custom welcome message shown to the candidate.

thank_you_message.description: Custom thank-you message shown after the interview.

microphone_test_message.description: Custom microphone-test instruction for a recorded (offline avatar) interview, spoken by the avatar and shown on screen before the first question. Omitted uses the default prompt in the interview language.
microphone_test_message.example: Before we start, let's check your microphone. Say "Hello, I'm ready."

microphone_test_no_speech_message.description: Custom text shown when the microphone test hears nothing. Omitted uses the default text in the candidate's language.
microphone_test_no_speech_message.example: We can't hear you. Check your microphone and try again.

additional_context.description: Arbitrary additional context object merged into AI generation.

instructional_video_custom_text.description: Custom narration text for the instructional video.

is_embedded.description: Set true when the interview will be embedded as an iframe on an external page. Provisions an embed key and returns embed_id / embed_signing_key, which are used to authenticate/sign the iframe embed. Where it runs depends on the type: interviews, assessments and interview role-plays embed on the interview portal (`https://<interview portal domain>/embed?embed_id=...`); coaching sessions and coaching personas embed on the consumer (coaching) portal (`https://<coaching portal domain>/embed?embed_id=...`, a link built on the interview portal is forwarded there). A signed coaching embed (name, email, signature) signs the visitor in as a learner of that portal, and the session is charged to the merchant's interview credits on completion, not to the learner's coaching credits; it cannot start while the merchant has none.

include_rapport_question.description: Include an opening rapport question. Defaults to false (true when questions is given).

include_closing_prompt.description: Include a closing prompt. Defaults to true.

instructional_video.description: Show an instructional video before approval. Defaults to false.

required_pronunciation.description: Require pronunciation assessment (restricts to pronunciation-capable languages). Defaults to false.

result_enable_edit_transcript.description: Allow editing the transcript on the result view. Defaults to true.

questions.description: OPTIONAL: your own ordered list of questions, in the format job-interview-get returns. When given, they are stored as written and nothing is generated by AI except the candidate expectations (type interview, unless candidate_expectations_json is given); in the session the avatar still says each question in the interview tone unless interview_tone is exact. With questions, description becomes required; interview_length and include_closing_prompt are ignored; include_rapport_question defaults to true; max_duration keeps its meaning here (stored, 1200 when omitted). Omit to have the AI generate the description and questions.

weak.description: Baseline requirements every viable candidate should meet (table stakes).

moderate.description: Requirements expected of a solid, competent candidate.

strong.description: High-bar requirements only standout candidates clear.

candidate_expectations_json.description: With questions only: pre-generated candidate expectations, bucketed by requirement level (weak/moderate/strong); generated from your questions when omitted for type interview. Ignored without questions.

disable_deduplication.description: With questions only: when true, every question is stored as a new record instead of reusing an identical one. Ignored without questions.

interview_category.description: Job category shown on public listings, above the department (free text, e.g. "Ashore"). Blank is stored as null.

welcome_message.example: Welcome! You are about to speak with a customer who is unhappy about a recent price increase.

thank_you_message.description: Custom thank-you message shown after the session — set it; omitting it leaves a generic platform default.
thank_you_message.example: Thanks — your role-play has been recorded and will be reviewed by the hiring team.

tags.description: Free-form tags stored on the persona. Tags are also the coaching-catalogue mapping key: a catalogue directory (see the catalogue-tag-create / catalogue-tag-update endpoints) lists a coaching or persona session when the session's tags contain EVERY tag in that directory's `tags_interview_set_filter`. Only `active` sessions with visibility `merchant_public` (or the platform's own `public`) are listed.

portal.description: REQUIRED IN PRACTICE — pick deliberately; the default is the coaching product, not the recruiting one. `interview`: an interview role-play. Choose this for ANY recruiting or assessment use case (screening candidates, hiring, sales role-plays for applicants). Candidates are invited through the normal invitation flow, results are visible to the recruiter alongside ordinary interview results, it is billed against your merchant credits on the same basis as an interview, and attempts are capped (see `interview_attempts`). | `coaching` (DEFAULT when omitted): the classic coaching persona for practice/training. Runs on the coaching portal, is consumed against the mentee's own coaching credits, is started by the mentee from the catalogue or a shared link, and its results are NOT visible to recruiters. The conversation itself behaves identically in both cases — only the portal, billing, visibility and attempt limits differ.
portal.x-mcp-description: Pick deliberately; left out, it is `coaching`. Values: `interview`: a scored role-play a recruiter invites candidates to, billed to merchant credits, attempts capped | `coaching`: a practice persona learners start from the catalogue, paid from their own coaching minutes, never visible to recruiters.

interview_attempts.description: Allowed candidate attempts (1-20), defaulting to 3. Only meaningful when `portal` is `interview`; coaching personas are unlimited. A recruiter can still grant an extra attempt afterwards.

is_embedded.description: Set true when the persona will be embedded as an iframe on an external page. Provisions an embed key and returns embed_id / embed_signing_key, used to sign the iframe link. Where it runs depends on the type: interviews, assessments and interview role-plays embed on the interview portal (`https://<interview portal domain>/embed?embed_id=...`); coaching sessions and coaching personas embed on the consumer (coaching) portal (`https://<coaching portal domain>/embed?embed_id=...`, a link built on the interview portal is forwarded there). A signed coaching embed (name, email, signature) signs the visitor in as a learner of that portal, and the session is charged to the merchant's interview credits on completion, not to the learner's coaching credits; it cannot start while the merchant has none.

accept_stage_id.description: ATS stage (Kombo id) a candidate moves to when accepted on this step. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

reject_reason_id.description: ATS rejection reason (Kombo id) used when a recruiter rejects on this step. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

reject_reason_ai_id.description: ATS rejection reason (Kombo id) used when the AI rejects on this step. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

mode.description: How candidates book: slots (hand-made slots, the default; add them with manage_meeting_slot) or availability (free times of the interviewers). null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

location.description: Address or room shown to the candidate when a slot has none. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

conference_provider.description: The meeting link: in_person (no link), fixed (meeting_url), zoom / teams / meet (made at booking with the interviewer's own calendar account, meeting_url is the fallback). Absent: fixed when meeting_url is set, else in_person. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

meeting_url.description: Video link (http or https) used when a slot has none. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

instructions.description: Instructions shown to the candidate. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

reschedule_cutoff_hours.description: Hours before the meeting after which the candidate can no longer reschedule or cancel (default 24). null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

interviewer_profile_ids.description: Availability mode: the interviewers whose free times are offered (profile.id of users of the company); empty = the position's recruiter. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

panel_profile_ids.description: Availability mode, company feature meeting_panels: a panel of 2 to 8 users who all attend (profile.id); the first leads the meeting and cannot be a read-only user. Candidates are offered only times when everyone is free. null = one interviewer. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

slot_interval_minutes.description: Availability mode: start times every N minutes, 5 to 240 (default 30). null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

min_notice_hours.description: Availability mode: earliest booking, hours from now, 0 to 720 (default 12). null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

horizon_days.description: Availability mode: latest booking, days from now, 1 to 365 (default 21). null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

mode.description: none, form (a meeting form, taxonomy_id) or text (free notes).

data_collection.description: What the interviewer records after the meeting. Replaced as a whole. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

email_variant.description: Needs the meeting_email_variants feature: the name of the e-mail version used for this step's meeting e-mails. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

provider_id.description: An active assessment provider of this company, set up in the admin (a step's current one is in job-interview-get include=process). Required on a new step.

instructions.description: Shown to the candidate (falls back to the provider's instructions). null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

due_days.description: Days the candidate has to finish, 1 to 60 (default 7).

pass_score.description: Optional pass mark: a result without a pass flag passes when its score is at least this. null removes the setting (its default applies again); left out keeps it.

collect_resume_cover_letter.description: Ask the candidate for a resume / cover letter: hidden, optional or required. Single-stage interviews only.

allow_human_interview.description: A recruiter may hold the interview instead of the AI. Single-stage interviews only (an interview step of a position carries its own setting, see merchant-position-step-update).

team.description: Multi-stage positions only (422 on an interview): the complete hiring team you want, replacing the current members (viewers, managed with position access, are kept). An empty array removes everyone. Needs the hiring team switched on for the company (else 403) and access to the position. Each member is a person (profile_id: an active or invited staff user of the company) or a group (profile_group_id), with a role. The answer carries the resulting `team`.

custom_fields.description: Company-defined position fields to set, {key: value}; a null value clears that field and keys you omit keep their value. Values are checked against the field definitions (option values, YYYY-MM-DD dates, {min, max, currency} ranges, user profile ids). Requires custom fields to be enabled for the company (else 403). Multi-stage positions only: on a single-stage interview the request is refused with 422.

questions.description: OPTIONAL. Omit this field entirely and the interview's questions are left exactly as they are — questions are only touched when you send the array. When you do send it, send the COMPLETE list you want the interview to end up with, in order, in the same format job-interview-create-from-array accepts and job-interview-get returns: there is no way to change a single question on its own, so read the interview, edit that array, and send the whole thing back. An empty array is rejected. It is applied as a DIFF, not a replace, so resending the array job-interview-get gave you changes nothing at all. Each entry is matched against what is stored — first on `external_id`, then on `id`, then on identical content — and: an entry matching an unchanged question keeps that question exactly as it is, including its answer rules and any rendered avatar video; an entry matching a question whose content differs unlinks the old question and creates a new one in its place (fields you omit are carried over from the old one); an entry matching nothing is created; and a stored question no entry matches is unlinked. `questions_diff` in the response reports exactly what was decided. Questions are shared records, so nothing is ever deleted — removing one only unlinks it from this interview, and an edit is always unlink-old + create-new so the change cannot leak into another interview reusing the same question. The welcome, thank-you and instructional-video steps are not part of this array and are left in place. Single-stage interviews only; for a multi-stage position, update its interview stages individually.

regenerate_candidate_expectations.description: Re-derive the interview-level `candidate_expectations_json` scoring rubric from the resulting question list, the way job-interview-create-from-array derives it at creation time. Only applies when `questions` is sent, the interview type is `interview`, and `candidate_expectations_json` is not also being set explicitly (an explicit value wins).

type.description: Product type of the interview. Changing it also re-derives `type_credit` (null for interview/assessment, otherwise interview_coach_manager) unless you send `type_credit` explicitly. Single-stage interviews only.

type_credit.description: Credit bucket the session draws from. Only meaningful for candidate-paid coaching/persona sessions; hiring interviews and assessments are merchant-billed and carry null. Options — `resume_check`: Resume Builder credits. | `interview_coach_starter`: Coaching credits — starter tier. | `interview_coach_contributor`: Coaching credits — contributor tier. | `interview_coach_manager`: Coaching credits — manager tier. | `cover_letter`: Cover-letter credits.

coach_plan.description: Coaching-plan stage this item belongs to, used by the coaching-plan progress view. Omit/null to leave it out of any plan. Options — `demo`: Demo session. | `screening`: Screening-interview practice. | `2nd`: Second-interview practice. | `3rd`: Third-interview practice. | `closing`: Closing / salary-negotiation practice. | `job-specific`: Job-specific coaching. | `other`: Anything that does not fit the other buckets.

interview_template_id.description: Id of the interview template (avatar/voice) to use. An id from merchant-avatar-list. Also decides the modality: see merchant-avatar-list.

knowledge_base_store_id.description: Knowledge base store id the interview draws context from; validated for existence. null unlinks it.

recording.description: Cheating/proctoring detection mode for candidate answers — this is NOT a full session recording. Video options also record the candidate. Omit to keep the current mode; `none` switches it off (null does too). Options — `audio_first_5_answers`: Audio-only cheating detection, first 5 answers only. | `audio_all`: Audio-only cheating detection on every answer. | `video_all`: Audio + video cheating detection on every answer (candidate is recorded for all answers). | `video_first_5_answers`: Audio + video cheating detection, first 5 answers only. | `none`: Switch cheating detection off.

recording_full_session.description: Full interview-session recording (includes the avatar and voice) produced as a single file. Independent of `recording`. Omit to keep the current setting; `none` switches it off (null does too). Options — `audio_all`: Record the whole session audio (avatar + candidate voice) into a single file. A new brand needs `name`; `slug` is optional, a short name kept for older links that decides no page address (two brands cannot share one). post.summary: Create a role-play — coaching persona or interview-portal role-play (choose with `portal`)
post.description:
FIRST DECIDE `portal`. This endpoint creates two different products and the default is NOT the recruiter one:
- `portal: "interview"` — an INTERVIEW ROLE-PLAY. Use this whenever the goal is to ASSESS or SCREEN candidates: hiring, assessments, sales role-plays for job applicants, anything a recruiter runs. Candidates are invited through the normal invitation flow, results appear in the recruiter's result list, it is billed against merchant credits, and attempts are capped via `interview_attempts` — exactly like an interview.
- `portal: "coaching"` (THE DEFAULT) — a coaching persona for practice/training on the coaching portal. Consumed against the mentee's own coaching credits, self-started from the catalogue, and its results are NOT visible to recruiters. Omitting `portal` gives you this one, so pass `portal: "interview"` explicitly for any recruiting/assessment use case.
The conversation itself behaves identically in both.

The avatar plays a defined role in a free-form conversation instead of running a scored Q&A interview. No AI question/description generation runs; the persona role fields ARE the configuration. The session runs as: a welcome message → the avatar's OPENING LINE (the first thing it says, set via `opening_line`) → the candidate replies and the free-form role-play begins → a closing message. Because there is no question list, `opening_line` is how the avatar starts the scene — set it to a concrete in-character line; if omitted it defaults to a generic "Hello". Set `welcome_message` and `thank_you_message` too — omitting them leaves the generic platform defaults. Also set `candidate_expectations`: it is the yardstick the session is scored against. The four avatar prompts divide up as: `persona_avatar_who_is` (identity and what drives it), `persona_avatar_knowledge` (the private facts it may use), `persona_avatar_progress` (how the conversation is allowed to move forward, and what gates the later personal details), and `persona_avatar_end_conditions` (when to stop). Without `persona_avatar_progress` the avatar has no defined arc and tends to either concede immediately or never concede at all. Provisions the default conversational steps and optionally an embed key.

For a multi-stage position, `include` adds the process steps (with meeting slots), the hiring team, the vacancy lifecycle with openings, and the publishing window. post.description: Updates the configuration of an existing interview (single-stage) or position (multi-stage). Only the fields present in the request body are written — everything else keeps its current value, and sending null clears a nullable field. The question list is only touched when you send `questions`; omit that field and the questions are left exactly as they are. When sent, it must be the complete list and is applied as a diff against what is stored (matched on external_id, then id, then identical content), so unchanged questions keep their existing records, edited ones are unlinked and re-created, and dropped ones are unlinked — and re-sending the array job-interview-get returned changes nothing. See the field description, and `questions_diff` in the response for what was decided. Questions of an interview that is already `active` can only be changed on interactive avatar templates, where re-publishing is instant; on the offline (pre-rendered video) templates set the interview back to `draft` first. The welcome / thank-you messages and the instructional-video screen are stored as steps rather than questions and are never changed here. `mojito_language_code` cannot be changed — the existing questions and rendered videos are in the original language — so create a new interview to change language. A multi-stage position only carries the shared identity fields (name, code, location, description, description_long, cover_image_url, department, salary, available_till, recruiter, status, visibility, hiring_for_company, tags, interview_category, emoji, custom_fields) and its hiring `team`; sending an interview-only field for a position is a 422.
